sections.h2: Which offices deal with a Whitley County tax bill?
sections.html: Whitley County splits the job three ways. The valuation administrator, called the PVA, sets each parcel's value, the sheriff mails and collects the bill, and the county clerk handles whatever is still open in spring. Call Property Valuation at (606) 549-6008 or 6009 and the sheriff at (606) 549-6006 or 6007. County offices share the courthouse at 200 Main Street, Williamsburg, and the sheriff's site has a bill lookup. The lookup opens your bill in a pop-up window, so switch off your browser's pop-up blocker before you search.

Home prices run low here. The middle owned home is valued at $131,800, and the typical household brings in $44,615 a year. Roughly two of every three households own where they live, and the county's 2025 estimate of 37,297 residents is 1.6 percent above 2020. Williamsburg is the seat and Corbin is the biggest city, reaching into Knox and Laurel counties.

  • Housing units on the July 2025 count: 15,904.
  • Typical rent: $798 a month.
  • Monthly costs for owners: $1,156 with a mortgage, $346 without.
  • Permits for new homes in 2025: only 52.

With so few new homes going up, a seller mostly competes with other resales. Corbin and Williamsburg are the two places with retail alcohol sales, and the county is otherwise classed as moist. The University of the Cumberlands is in Williamsburg.

sections.h2: What happens when a Whitley County bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
The state schedule in KRS 134.015 runs from a 2 percent discount by November 1 to a 10 percent penalty after January. Whoever owned the house on January 1 owes that year's bill personally, so a spring closing does not erase it.

When the sheriff is still unpaid on April 15, the clerk receives the bill, records a lien and files it as a delinquency certificate. From then on 1 percent interest accrues monthly, the clerk adds 10 percent and the county attorney adds 20 percent. The lien follows the parcel for up to 11 years, whoever buys it.

Whitley's clerk then sells the debt to private buyers in a September sale. Terms for the 2025 bills are in the table.

Whitley County Clerk terms for the 2025 tax bill sale
Sale termRule
Time and place9:00 a.m., courthouse Room 2
FormatLottery, up to three bills per buyer
Registration fee$10 per certificate, capped at $250 for 25 or more
Deposit25 percent of the certificates listed

The clerk takes no payments on the morning of the sale. Whoever buys your certificate collects from you and may add fees. Call the clerk for the date of the next sale.

Buyers with a stake in an earlier year can file a priority list, which needs a $5 fee per certificate and a deposit of the full price, and every certificate carries a $30 filing charge. A buyer who wants more than three certificates in the county, more than five statewide or more than $10,000 worth must also enroll with the state revenue department. A seller with a delinquent parcel should clear it with the clerk before the sale date, because paying off the lien is cheaper than paying a buyer who tacks on fees.

sections.h2: How to contest a Whitley County assessment
sections.html:
Meet the PVA first, since Kentucky bars an appeal without that meeting. Values are fixed as of January 1, the roll lies open to the public for 13 days starting with the first May Monday, and the meeting belongs inside that stretch.

Then file with the County Clerk no later than the following workday. A local board hears the case 25 to 35 days later and dismisses anything that comes without proof.

  • Recent sales of nearby houses like yours.
  • Photos and repair quotes where the house has defects the record misses.
  • Insurance or construction cost papers.

Before you file, ask which sales the PVA used on your parcel.

Homeowners at least 65 years old, and the totally disabled, subtract a fixed amount from the assessed value of the home they live in. A couple gets one deduction. File form 62A350 at the PVA office; an approved claim carries forward while the same owner stays. A buyer must apply again, and the PVA can quote the current deduction, which the state resets every two years.

If you are selling, mention it to your buyer early. Someone who qualifies will want to visit the PVA after closing, and the exemption is not something that transfers with the deed.

sections.h2: How the tax year runs for a Whitley County owner
sections.html:
The roll is fixed as of January 1, and whoever owns the house on that date is the person billed. The sheriff mails bills in the fall. A payment in full by November 1 earns the 2 percent discount, the printed amount applies through the end of the year, and a 10 percent penalty applies after January. In spring the roll opens for 13 days beginning with the first May Monday, which is the time to question a value.

If you list the house in the winter or spring, ask the sheriff whether the current bill has been paid and what any penalty adds. A balance that has reached the clerk carries a lien, interest each month, and the clerk's and county attorney's percentages. Paying it before the September sale keeps a private buyer out of the picture.

Property Valuation at (606) 549-6008 or 6009 can tell you how the parcel is assessed, and the sheriff at (606) 549-6006 or 6007 can tell you what is owed.

sections.h2: What a Whitley County seller should confirm before closing
sections.html:
Treat the tax like a payoff, alongside any mortgage. The title company asks the sheriff and the clerk for balances, and both come out of what you receive.

  • Match the name on the bill to the deed.
  • Look for a bill on a garage, mobile home or other addition missing from earlier rolls.
  • On an inherited house, check whether the bill was mailed to someone who has died.
  • Ask the clerk if an earlier year was sold to a private buyer.

Get each balance in writing so the payoff matches the closing statement.

A cash sale can handle a messy tax history without much delay. If a certificate has already gone to a private buyer, the payoff comes from that buyer instead of the clerk, and it includes the buyer's fees. Ask the title company to order the figure early so it is not a surprise at the table.

faqs.q: Where does a Whitley County owner send the tax payment?
faqs.a: To the sheriff, whose site offers an online lookup and whose office is at (606) 549-6006 or 6007. After April 15 the bill sits with the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Is it too late to pay a Whitley County bill after January?
faqs.a: No, but the cost rises. A 10 percent penalty applies after January, and after April 15 monthly interest and commissions come on top.

faqs.q: Can a Whitley County owner sell with a delinquent bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company gets the figures from the sheriff and clerk, and the balance is subtracted from what you receive. The lien stays until it is cleared.

faqs.q: When must a Whitley County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: No later than the workday after the roll inspection ends. The roll opens for 13 days beginning the first May Monday, and you must meet the PVA before filing.

faqs.q: Which Whitley County office answers valuation questions?
faqs.a: Property Valuation, at (606) 549-6008 or 6009. The sheriff covers the amount due, and the clerk covers delinquent bills.
